name: Resilient 72-hour Support Node
location_context: Dispersed support node, temperate northern Europe, late autumn. Road access for one resupply vehicle. SYNTHETIC scenario, not a real location.

grid_availability.note: SYNTHETIC. Host-nation supply assumed present on arrival, lost at H+14, restored H+30, lost again at H+44 for the remainder of the mission.

weather_profile.description: Temperate northern Europe, late autumn, variable cloud (SYNTHETIC)

mobility_requirement.note: The node is not required to relocate during this mission. Assets that could not move within 120 minutes are listed separately so the operator can see what a relocation order would cost.

operator_priorities.statement: Command, IT and medical support must remain available for the full 72 hours.
Keep equipment shelters within thermal limits; a degraded setpoint is acceptable if it buys endurance.
Keep UAS charging available if it does not threaten critical functions.
Minimise fuel resupply exposure; no resupply is assumed within the mission.
Vehicle charging and welfare HVAC are discretionary.

notes: MM-DEMO-001 is an invented scenario written to exercise the planner. It does not reflect any armed forces requirement, doctrine, or real deployment.

Fuel limit of 520 L is the total bulk fuel on site; no resupply is assumed to arrive during the mission. The figure is chosen so that the mission is achievable but not comfortable - that is where the trade-offs become visible.
No adversary behaviour is modelled. Disruption is represented only as asset unavailability.
